key_insight: More training data often improves tabular models, but under distribution shift, in-distribution gains can diverge from out-of-distribution performance at larger scales.
engineering_relevance: For deployment under distribution shift, scale training data alongside evaluation-representative validation rather than assuming larger datasets guarantee better generalization.
method: Study training-data scaling across eight real-world tabular datasets, preserving natural shifts and using random splits as controls.
Compare GBDTs, MLP-based models, and tabular foundation models across data scales.
Examine MLP capacity, validation distributions for tuning and early stopping, and foundation-model context composition.
evidence_signal: Across datasets with up to around 10 million training examples, GBDTs and MLPs show broadly similar scaling trends, while foundation-model behavior is more varied.
watch_item: Under stronger shifts, adding evaluation-representative examples to foundation-model contexts improves performance but does not prevent deterioration as training size grows in these experiments.
paper_title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
